strings.read:
{1c:10}毒術師について語る前に、
私の生まれた民族、
セディクについて話をさせて下さい。{1a}セディク族は
ルミニア北西部の少数民族です。{1a}太古の昔からその地は
作物の実り少ない痩せた地域で
あったため、{1a}私達の先祖は生き延びるために
部族内で何千年も受け継がれてきた
毒の技術を利用することを考えました。{1a}すなわち、セディク族に伝わる
毒草や薬草の知識を生かし、
他の土地で生きることを
決意したのです。{1a}同時に、自分たちを高く売るため、
セディク族に伝わる技術を
族内のみの秘伝としました。{1a}他と比べると遙かに高度な
医療技術を持つことから、
貴族や教会などの権力者も
セディクの力を必要としはじめます。{1a}セディク族はいつしか単なる
少数民族ではなく、特殊な技術を
代々受け継ぐ秘密結社的な性格を
色濃く持ち始めます。{1a}私達セディク族が『毒殺者』と呼ばれ
恐れられ、同時に蔑まれているのも、
こういった秘密主義に
深く関係があるのでしょう。{1a}実際には毒で要人を暗殺することなど
ほとんどなかったのですが、
権力に擦り寄る我々への反発と、{1a}得体の知れない術を使う我々への
恐怖心からか、私達セディク族には
常に『死』のイメージが
つきまとうこととなります。{0c:040d}
strings.en:
{1c:10}Before I speak of poisoners, please allow
me to speak of the people into which I
was born, the Sedik.{1a}The Sedik are a minority people of
northwestern Luminia.{1a}Since ancient times that land has been
barren, with few crops to bear,{1a}so to survive, our ancestors thought to
use the arts of poison handed down
within the tribe for thousands of years.{1a}That is, they resolved to live in other
lands by making use of the Sedik
knowledge of poisonous and medicinal
herbs.{1a}At the same time, to sell themselves at
a high price, they made the arts of the
Sedik a secret kept only within the tribe.{1a}Because they held medical arts far more
advanced than any other, nobles, the
Church and others in power began to
need the strength of the Sedik.{1a}In time the Sedik took on the strong
character not merely of a minority
people, but of a secret society handing
down special arts from one generation{1a}to the next.{1a}That we Sedik are called 'Poison Killers',
feared and at the same time despised,
no doubt has much to do with this
secrecy.{1a}In truth, we almost never assassinated
great persons with poison, but from
resentment of how we curried favor
with power,{1a}and from fear of those who use
unknowable arts, the image of 'Death'
has clung to the Sedik ever since.{0c:040d}
strings.tl: Before I speak of poisoners, please allow me to speak of the people into which I was born, the Sedik. // The Sedik are a minority people of northwestern Luminia. // Since ancient times that land has been barren, with few crops to bear, // so to survive, our ancestors thought to use the arts of poison handed down within the tribe for thousands of years. // That is, they resolved to live in other lands by making use of the Sedik knowledge of poisonous and medicinal herbs. // At the same time, to sell themselves at a high price, they made the arts of the Sedik a secret kept only within the tribe. // Because they held medical arts far more advanced than any other, nobles, the Church and others in power began to need the strength of the Sedik. // In time the Sedik took on the strong character not merely of a minority people, but of a secret society handing down special arts from one generation to the next. // That we Sedik are called 'Poison Killers', feared and at the same time despised, no doubt has much to do with this secrecy. // In truth, we almost never assassinated great persons with poison, but from resentment of how we curried favor with power, // and from fear of those who use unknowable arts, the image of 'Death' has clung to the Sedik ever since.

strings.en:
{1c:10}About me, you say...?{1a}My father was the chief who ruled two
thousand of the Sedik.{1a}He came to doubt the closed laws of the
Sedik,{1a}and from his conviction that 'to save
more people from sickness, the Sedik
arts held as secret must be made public',{1a}he began to reveal the arts of the Sedik
to outsiders.{1a}But when I was eight years old, my
father was assassinated by
conservatives who hated his ideas.{1a}I left Luminia and fled to an
acquaintance of my father in Asroit.{1a}However, when I was fourteen, the one
who had sheltered me also fell ill.{1a}With my benefactor's death as the
turning point, I came to this town with
Fatum-san and Nada-san, whom I had
met in Asroit.{1a}I came here to escape assassins of my
own people, who seek my life even now.{0c:040d}
strings.tl: About me, you say...? // My father was the chief who ruled two thousand of the Sedik. // He came to doubt the closed laws of the Sedik, // and from his conviction that 'to save more people from sickness, the Sedik arts held as secret must be made public', // he began to reveal the arts of the Sedik to outsiders. // But when I was eight years old, my father was assassinated by conservatives who hated his ideas. // I left Luminia and fled to an acquaintance of my father in Asroit. // However, when I was fourteen, the one who had sheltered me also fell ill. // With my benefactor's death as the turning point, I came to this town with Fatum-san and Nada-san, whom I had met in Asroit. // I came here to escape assassins of my own people, who seek my life even now.

strings.en:
{1c:10}Of the six who became Berserkers, two
have, regrettably, already lost their
lives...{1a}Those harmed this time are by no means
few.{1a}Even so, it came to less than half of the
last incident. For now, let us be thankful
for that...{1a}You found that sword in the First
Temple, I hear,{1a}but the very first to awaken reportedly
found it inside a building called the
'Tower of Light', far deeper within,{1a}and the last to become a Berserker,
according to one who was with that
person until just before, found it in an
entirely different place.{1a}Whether the ten who have become
Berserkers so far have anything in
common, or whether it is pure chance, I
do not know.{1a}But this much is certain: you did not
become so by your own wish.{1a}Feeling against you will remain strong.
Yet you need not feel too heavily the
responsibility of having hurt others.{1a}Rather, keep in your heart only the
responsibility of saving your friends who
have not yet woken.{1a}These are my benefactor's words: the
strong do not bemoan their fate.{0c:040d}

For now, let us be thankful for that... // You found that sword in the First Temple, I hear, // but the very first to awaken reportedly found it inside a building called the 'Tower of Light', far deeper within, // and the last to become a Berserker, according to one who was with that person until just before, found it in an entirely different place. // Whether the ten who have become Berserkers so far have anything in common, or whether it is pure chance, I do not know. // But this much is certain: you did not become so by your own wish. // Feeling against you will remain strong. Yet you need not feel too heavily the responsibility of having hurt others. // Rather, keep in your heart only the responsibility of saving your friends who have not yet woken. // These are my benefactor's words: the strong do not bemoan their fate.

strings.en:
{1c:11}It is a dull old story, but please hear me...{1a}When I was eight years old, my father,
chief of the Sedik, was assassinated by
his younger brother, my uncle...{1a}Then, to escape the hands of my uncle,
who had taken the chief's seat,{1a}I fled to my father's friend Habash,
poisoner to the royal court of the
Kingdom of Asroit...{1a}Three years later, by chance, I learned
of Fatum-san and Nada-san.{1a}A sister and brother about my age,
confined for over twenty years in a dark
dungeon no light could reach, I heard...{1a}I asked the poisoner Habash, who had a
political voice, and he had the two of
them rescued from the dungeon...{1a}My first impression of them was very
poor.{1a}I had expected words of thanks, but
Fatum-san only glanced at me and shut
himself in his room.{1a}I was truly a foolish child...{1a}Drunk on my hypocritical deed, I never
once considered how Fatum-san felt...{1a}Three more years passed after that...
When I was fourteen, my benefactor
Habash, who had sheltered me, also left
this world.{1a}Whether my uncle killed him or he died a
natural death, I do not know.{1a}In any case, as his last will directed, I set
out for this town, taking Fatum-san and
Nada-san with me...{1a}I, aged fourteen, Fatum-san, with the
look of fifteen, and Nada-san, who would
never wake:{1a}for the three of us, that flight was by
no means easy.{1a}Before we reached this town, we were
attacked three times, and three times
Fatum-san saved my life...{1a}And yet, even now, I have repaid nothing
of that debt...{1a}I cannot save Nada-san, and I cannot be
a support to Fatum-san's heart...{1a}How I resent my own powerlessness...{0c:040d}

When I was fourteen, my benefactor Habash, who had sheltered me, also left this world. // Whether my uncle killed him or he died a natural death, I do not know. // In any case, as his last will directed, I set out for this town, taking Fatum-san and Nada-san with me... // I, aged fourteen, Fatum-san, with the look of fifteen, and Nada-san, who would never wake: // for the three of us, that flight was by no means easy. // Before we reached this town, we were attacked three times, and three times Fatum-san saved my life... // And yet, even now, I have repaid nothing of that debt... // I cannot save Nada-san, and I cannot be a support to Fatum-san's heart... // How I resent my own powerlessness...

strings.en:
{1c:10}Because life is limited, people can
respect and love others...{1a}Since the 'Azare Stone' was found,
writers have grown fond of such words.{1a}They may be the truth. But I cannot
bring myself to like them...{1a}The anguish of those with eternal life...
The looks of envy, jealousy and hatred,{1a}the loneliness of being unable to share
time with anyone... and then... eternal
darkness...{1a}They suffer too... They suffer precisely
because they love others...{1a}I... I am relieved that the 'Azare Stone' is
not the treasure everyone imagines...{0c:040d}
